body:
Thanks for opening this issue. As already expressed before I do currently not have the capacity or motivation to fix yet another libmariadb specific problem. Form my point of view using this library is not support and might therefore fail with whatever error. 

That doesn't mean I will reject an fix, but it means I won't fix that problem.

Well, in this case the previous version of Diesel works fine.
I'm not sure if this should now count as a regression. But, the latest version is just not workable at all.

Again, not yet dived into it though.

It might sound harsh, but that's exactly what "Not supported" means. We don't test against this platform (libmariadb) and therefore don't give any guarantees that something continues to work. Basically consider having the same guarantees as for a rust tier 3 target: It's there and it might work. If not we are happy to accept a fix from the community. If it's broken for too long it will be removed entirely.
Now there is certainly also a way to discuss changing the support status in some way, but that would involve that someone steps up and actually says: I'm responsible for maintaining this. I do not have the capacity for this and I also don't use this backend at all. If someone want's to step up doing this I'm happy to discuss the next steps.

I also want to clarify that I don't expect you personally to take this additional load, it's just important for me to draw a line what's actually supported and what not.

I fully understand, so no prob there. I only thought that since this seems to break much more now, you might want to decide to revert it maybe.

Might need to look at that other solution you mentioned for this backend.

- Updated all the crates except for Diesel.
  Diesel is pinned at v2.3.3 since newer versions break MySQL/MariaDB. (See https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/issues/4889)
- Updated all the GHA workflows
- Fixed an issue with a migration breaking on an empty MySQL/MariaDB database.

body: @weiznich, just for clarification regarding the not supported, is that only regarding `libmariadb` a.k.a. MariaDB Connector/C or also `libmysqlcient` the C API part of the MySQL Server code?

I consider libmysqlclient as supported. In the end it boils down to whatever we use in CI and what's tested there. 

I had a short look at the exact failure: The relevant assert is here: 

https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/main/diesel/src/mysql/connection/bind.rs#L430-L435

It is supposed to verify that the underlying buffer is initialised on rust side with zeroed memory for at least the buffer side. Given that the capacity of the buffer matches what's expected but the size not, it seems like it still misses a branch somewhere. This initialisation was added as additional safety layer as we don't know how may bytes libmariadb initialises. By setting the buffer to all zero in the beginning at least we don't expose uninitialised memory if something goes wrong again of their side. 

So a potential fix would need to track down where this initialisation is missing. As "workaround" you might be able to just compile diesel in release mode to disable the assert. Obviously that just skips the check that might point to an actual problem

Ok, small side-note, I'm trying a different route here to try and use the bundled mysqlclient, but without openssl as a vendored feature. It's a Work In Progress https://github.com/BlackDex/mysqlclient-sys/actions/runs/19803810192/job/56734910918 Only having some issues with the Windows builds.

issue.title: Another mariadb fix

repository.name: diesel
repository.description: A safe, extensible ORM and Query Builder for Rust

issue.body:
This commit fixes another issue with libmariadb. In this case again the libmariadb documentation/behaviour is inconsistent. They stated that with the last version they won't set the lenght field for statically sized types. Turns out that even that is not correct, as it is set for the datetime type. Now this on it's own wouldn't be an issue, but libmariadb has a slightly different definition of `MYSQL_TIME` that libmysqlclient. It misses a field in the end. While this is normally not a problem as that field is just zero initialized by diesel, it becomes problematic if libmariadb returns the size of their definition, which results in the assert mentioned in the issue to fail. So it's yet another needless incompatiblity on their side we need to workaround.

Fixes #4889

cc @BlackDex It would be great to know if the fix works for you. As already written in #4889 we should find a better solution for testing and maintaining support for libmariadb in the future. Possibly it would already help if someone sets up at least one CI job that runs tests with libmariadb + mariadb instead of libmysqlclient + mysql and also if someone at least helps looking into issues that come up. To be upfront here: If the situation around the mysql/mariadb backend doesn't change much in the next year or so, I consider issuing a diesel 3.0 release that moves this backend out of tree and marks it as unmaintained by me.
